text_post: I avoid Facebook like the plague, I don't know what would have happened if I didn't.  That said, I see the utility; it honestly can be a good tool for keeping in touch with distant friends because you can simply publish what's going on and everyone can read it.  But in that, we lose the basic human interaction.  I'd much rather my friend call me and tell me about his trip to Romania than just slap it online and expect me to drool over the pictures.  If we're talking about it it builds the relationship; published it's almost like background noise. I think Facebook feeds anxiety in people too.  I think people post all the tiny little "best-moment' snapshots of their life on there and anxious people are sitting back thinking "Fuck, my life isn't anywhere near as good as so-and-so's" when in fact so-and-so is a 3-bottle a day alcoholic and about to be fired from their job.  It creates an unrealistic picture of people's lives and in anxious people likely to make the comparison, an unrealistic expectation for what their lives should be like.
